records.title: International Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), COLREGs, ILC State Responsibility, ICJ 'Critical Date' Sovereignty & EEZ/ADIZ Airspace Law (CMGZ-P1 Ch. 4, CAP-P2 Ch. 6)
records.author_org: CDR Jonathan G. Odom, JAGC, USN & Prof. Peter A. Dutton (USNWC CMSI) / UNCLOS (1982), Chicago Convention (1944), COLREGs (1972), ILC (2001) & South China Sea Arbitral Tribunal (July 12, 2016)
records.type: Public International Law, Treaty Jurisprudence & Arbitral Awards on Maritime/Airspace Operations
records.description: Synthesizes Odom's and Dutton's legal analyses arguing, subject to the facts and legal conditions in each case, that (1) CCG and PAFMM actions are attributable to the PRC under ILC State Responsibility Articles 4, 5, and 8; (2) post-'critical date' gray-zone actions are legally 'meaningless' for improving territorial sovereignty claims under ICJ jurisprudence; (3) PAFMM/CCG harassment violates UNCLOS Arts. 56, 58, and 94 and COLREGs Rules 2, 6, 7, 8, 13, 15, 16, and 18 (confirmed in the July 12, 2016 Arbitral Award paras. 742, 1091, 1094, 1109); and (4) ADIZ regulations cannot lawfully restrict nonthreatening foreign military reconnaissance flights in international airspace above the EEZ.
records.use_description:
The papers cite the instruments and scholarship to compare readings of jurisdiction, state responsibility, and maritime rights.

**Interpretive scope.** Treaty wording, a tribunal’s holding, and an author’s legal application are distinct. This collection does not establish that every later coast-guard action is attributable or unlawful without event-specific facts and legal analysis.

connection_review.finding: The supplied introduction summarizes Dutton and other contributors to the same gray-zone volume. This is editorial context, not an independent external corroboration.
CS21-P5 discusses international law and separately cites Dutton on the Han incident. That is not a citation of the later CAP-P2/CMGZ-P1 chapters collected here.
